primitives.name: Game Outcome Discriminant
primitives.verbatim_quote: A discriminant analysis was used to identify the performance indicators either in regular season and playoff games.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D': 'discriminant function value (dimensionless)', 'X': 'performance vector (assists, rebounds, FG%)', 'Y': 'outcome class (win/loss)'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear separability of performance classes; multivariate normality of predictors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Score margin > 28 points or low sample size (< 10 games).

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian posterior probability P(Y|X) derived from discriminant scores D(X).
layer2.telemetry: Classification accuracy of win/loss based on X.

primitives.name: Score Imbalance Cluster
primitives.verbatim_quote: A previous cluster analysis allowed splitting the sample in balanced (equal or below 12 points), unbalanced (between 13 and 28 points) and very unbalanced games (above 28 points).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'cluster label (balanced, unbalanced, very unbalanced)', 'ΔS': 'final score difference (points)'}
primitives.assumptions: Cluster centroids represent stable game dynamics; ΔS defines game intensity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: ΔS < 12 points or ΔS > 28 points with insufficient data.

layer2.mapping: GSE state space partitioning into C-regimes with distinct tactical behaviors.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of games in each ΔS category.

primitives.name: Defensive Rebound Superiority
primitives.verbatim_quote: However, in playoff games the winning teams' superiority was only in defensive rebounding.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'DR': 'defensive rebounds per game (dimensionless)', 'W': 'winning team indicator (0 or 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rebound rate correlates with possession control; playoff pressure increases defensive focus.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low DR variance or W=0 in sample.

layer2.mapping: GSI conditional expectation E[DR|W=1] exceeds baseline in playoff context.
layer2.telemetry: Mean DR difference between winning and losing teams.

The core mathematical structure emerges from discriminant analysis applied to basketball performance data. The discriminant function D(X) maps high-dimensional performance vectors X to binary outcomes Y. In regular season, D(X) is sensitive to assist and field goal success rates, reflecting strategic offensive dominance. In playoffs, D(X) becomes more sensitive to defensive rebounding, indicating a shift toward limiting opponent scoring. This dual behavior reflects a regime change in game dynamics—where regular season emphasizes offensive efficiency and playoff emphasis shifts to defensive resilience. The score imbalance clusters act as bifurcation parameters, altering the effective dimensionality of X. When ΔS ≤ 12, the game is balanced and D(X) operates under standard assumptions. When ΔS > 28, the game is unstable and D(X) fails due to reduced sample size and increased variance. The derived kernel in GSI encodes these regime-dependent mappings as Bayesian posteriors, while GSE uses the same kernels to model state transitions across game regimes.
